title: Bloodlust Optimizer catalog
description: Schema for catalog/catalog.json. This is a convenience for editors and CI: the authoritative validation is in sidecar/src/bloodlust/core/catalog.py, which additionally enforces the handler allowlist. Both must agree.

schema.description: Must match CATALOG_SCHEMA_VERSION in both the Python engine and the Rust bridge.

catalog_version.description: Free-form version shown in the UI. Bump it whenever the catalog changes so users can tell which one they have.

notice.description: Optional one-line message displayed with the provenance.

id.description: Lowercase snake_case. Used as the undo journal filename, so it must be filesystem-safe.

label.description: Shown in the UI. Describe the outcome, not the mechanism: 'Keep CPU at full clock', not 'Set PROCTHROTTLEMIN to 100'.

risk.description: Gated by the user's risk ceiling. 'aggressive' and above must also set default_enabled to false, so a batch run cannot apply them unasked.

handler.description: A function already compiled into the app, e.g. 'power.set_min_processor_state'. A catalog cannot introduce a new one; validation rejects the whole file if it tries.

description.description: Say what it does AND what it costs. Users read this before clicking Apply.

args.description: Primitives only. Validated again against the handler's own schema at runtime, so a value outside its declared range is rejected.

requires.description: Fail-closed: if a requirement cannot be verified on the machine, the action is blocked rather than allowed.

reversible.description: A statement of fact. Set false only for genuinely one-way actions like cache deletion.

default_enabled.description: Whether a batch run picks this up. Must be false for risk 'aggressive' and above.
